raw_response:
I am not farming many mu, only 7.5 mu, and there are just two people in the house, with some labor going off-farm, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest income here and I know this system well. Wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so my main job now is to hold the stand, give it one solid topdress and the key irrigations, and not get stingy at jointing. If wheat loses color in spring, yield drops fast, and on such a small farm I feel that loss more than the extra fertilizer bill. Maize will go in right after wheat harvest, with very little turnaround time, so I will keep tillage simple and use a hybrid seed I trust. I have a well, so I can protect the crop when rain does not come, but I will not over-irrigate because pumping costs money.

For kohlrabi, I will keep only a small area, 1.5 mu, because vegetables need more hands and more watching than grain. I can manage a small patch well, sell some fresh, and still not overload the household. Since I have more schooling and long experience, I do look at field condition and expected return, but I still farm in a practical way: round numbers, split fertilizer, and no fancy risk-taking. This year I would rather keep yields steady than chase the absolute maximum.
